newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikko Securities sees capital safety ratio falling.
newsitem.headline: Nikko Securities sees capital safety ratio falling.

text.p: Nikko Securities Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it expects its capital safety ratio to fall to 240 percent at the end of March 1997 from 350 percent at the end of September 1996 and 425 percent at the end of March 1996.
Earlier on Tuesday, Nikko announced that it would provide 147.5 billion yen in financial aid to its three non-bank affiliates.
The capital safety ratio is the ratio of net capital and latent profits on securities holdings and risk assets and possible losses from the securities business.

A ratio of below 150 percent is considered an early warning level and if it falls below 120 percent, financial authorities can order brokerages to improve their operations under the Securities and Exchange Law.
Masao Yuki, the vice president of Nikko Securities, told reporters that by providing financial aid to its three non-bank affiliates, the Nikko group would solve the group's problem asset woes.
Yuki also said that the broker has not made a decision on annual dividends. In the 1995/96 year ended March 31, 1996, Nikko paid eight yen in annual dividends.
